test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Is there any advantage of the structure of the nephron as a long tubular structure?

options.text: No, the long tubular structure has no advantage because filtration occurs at the cup-shaped end.
Yes, the long tubes can be coiled and packed at high density to give firmness to the kidney.
No, all nephrons are not long - some are short and others are long, but all are functional.
Yes, the long tube gives time and space for re-absorption of excess water from the initial filtrate.

solution:
The correct answer is ' **Yes, the long tube gives time and space for re-absorption of excess water from the initial filtrate.' **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The urine will be increasingly concentrated the further the nephron loop descends into the **medulla**.
 
• The renal medulla is home to the **lengthy nephron loops of the juxtamedullary nephrons**.
 
• An** osmotic gradient **is created and kept constant by these countercurrent mechanisms, ranging from the cortex to the medulla's deepest layers.
 
• Animals from the desert have longer Henle loops in their kidneys to increase urine concentration and reduce salt and water loss.
 
• This enables desert animals to survive for **extended periods of time** with little water.
 
• The Henle loop refers to this area of the nephron. Its major job is to reabsorb **sodium chloride and water from the filtrate**.
 
• By conserving water, the organism can produce **urine that is extremely concentrated**.
